common_name: Merlin Hellebore (Winter Jewels Series Silvery Purple Picotee Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Merlin is part of the Winter Jewels breeding series and shows a silvery, frosted purple picotee edge on its late-winter flowers.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, keeping soil evenly moist while the plant establishes. Merlin bears silvery lavender-purple flowers with a deeper picotee edge along the petal margins, part of the acclaimed Winter Jewels breeding series known for pushing hellebore color and pattern well beyond the plain pinks and whites of older seed strains. Like other Lenten roses it blooms very early, often pushing up through late-season snow or hard frost to provide color in the shade garden when little else is flowering. Remove tattered old foliage in late winter just before bloom to showcase the flowers, and site it away from areas where pets or children graze, since all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.
sources: Northwest Garden Nursery — Winter Jewels hellebore breeding

common_name: Molly's White Hellebore (Wedding Party Series Anemone-Centered White Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; part of the Wedding Party breeding series bred for showy, anemone-centered double flowers held well above the foliage.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, keeping soil evenly moist while the plant establishes. Molly's White bears pure white, anemone-centered flowers with a ring of small petaloids inside the outer sepals, held outward and upright rather than nodding, a trait bred into the Wedding Party series specifically so the flowers can be admired without tipping the bloom up to look inside as older downward-facing hellebores require. Like other Lenten roses it blooms very early, often through late-season snow or hard frost, providing bright color in the shade garden when little else is flowering. Remove tattered old foliage in late winter just before bloom to showcase the flowers, and site away from areas where pets or children graze, since all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.
sources: Walters Gardens — Wedding Party hellebore breeding
